items.title: 68357_Jimmy Maxwell oral history interview
items.q: And it was the surprise of my life when I left Benny's band.

ctx.x: But everything turned out. Her elder brother, you know, pushed people through and we got married. And my son was born -- we were married in '41 and my son was born two or three years later. So that's -- no, he was born four years later, '45. So Gertrude traveled with the band for two years and then I decided I wanted to have a family. And my teacher, Benny Baker, he was a former first trumpet player with the NBC symphony, he said he could get me a job in the staff orchestra at CBS and for me to quit Benny's band…
And it was the surprise of my life when I left Benny's band. Benny had me so buffaloed I didn't think anybody would hire me. And within a week of quitting the band it seemed

like everybody in the country offered -- Basie offered me a job. And I said, why didn't you ever ask me before, for God's sake? And he said, "I couldn't afford to pay you." And I said, "you've offered me $100.00 a week more than Benny's playing me." He said, "I don't believe it." And I said, "That's right."
